parameters.text:
=Today is {{ $now.setZone('Europe/Rome').toFormat('cccc d LLLL yyyy, HH:mm') }} (Europe/Rome).

Decide whether this email announces, or invites the recipient to, a specific scheduled EVENT they could attend: a webinar, live online session, conference, workshop, seminar, meetup, training course or class with concrete date(s) and start time(s).

NOT an event (isEvent = false):
- newsletters or promotions with no scheduled session; on-demand or recorded courses with no fixed time
- calendar-system messages (Google Calendar / Outlook invitations, "Invitation:", "Updated invitation", "Accepted:", "Declined:")
- a person asking to schedule a meeting with the recipient (handled elsewhere)
- events whose dates have already passed; receipts and confirmations of something already bought, unless they state an upcoming session time

For an event, list every session with start and end in ISO 8601 with the UTC offset, converted to Europe/Rome. If the email states another time zone, convert from it. If no end time is given, use the stated duration; otherwise assume 60 minutes and say so in notes. A multi-day course gets one session per day (max 10). Never invent a date or time that is not in the email: if the date or start time is missing, set isEvent = false.

eventType is one of: webinar, course, conference, workshop, seminar, meetup, event. title is the event's own name, not the email subject. link is the join or registration URL if present. summary is one factual sentence in the email's language.

Respond with ONLY the JSON object required by the schema.

parameters.content:
## Events, webinars, courses
Daily: scans the last 24h of the whole inbox (keyword pre-filter), asks Claude whether each email is a scheduled event, and checks the dates against your primary and Meetings calendars (all-day events count as busy).

For every new event it writes a Gmail **draft with no recipient**: FREE (add / ignore) or CONFLICT (keep / swap). The links go to **Gmail Assistant — Decisions**; nothing changes until you confirm there.

Every checked email is logged in **Inbox Pilot Decisions**, so it is never checked twice.

description: Sub-workflow: finds event/webinar/course emails from the last 24h, checks calendar availability, and drafts a FREE/CONFLICT decision note with add/ignore or keep/swap links.
